description: We are a passionate team from Sri Lanka, excited about AI, Machine Learning, Software Development, and Space Technology. Our goal is to solve real-world challenges through creativity, innovation, and teamwork. We're looking for enthusiastic members skilled in programming, UI/UX design, data analysis, research, and problem-solving. Whether you're a beginner or experienced, join us to learn, collaborate, and build something extraordinary together.
summary:
AEGIS BioOS is a local astronaut health-monitoring prototype. We developed an interactive body view for exploring recorded health readings, a dashboard for cabin conditions, a rule-based health review screen, and a tool for recording mood, stress, sleep, and fatigue. We also built Astra’s Garden, a 3D game where astronauts control a character, grow flowers, unlock new garden areas, and can optionally report their tension before and after playing.

The project addresses the challenge of keeping physical health and wellbeing information understandable and accessible during space missions, when support from Earth may not be immediate. Bringing these activities together could help crew members notice changes and seek support earlier, while making wellbeing activities more engaging. The current version uses simulated readings and is not a medical decision tool. Future work will connect approved vest measurements and exercise recommendations, then test whether the game helps astronauts feel less stressed.
details:
AEGIS BioOS is a prototype that brings astronaut health readings, cabin conditions, and wellbeing check-ins into one local application. AstroTwin shows health information on an interactive body view, BioSync displays cabin trends, AURA flags readings for review, and MindShield records how astronauts feel. Astra’s Garden adds a controllable 3D character and a gardening activity with optional tension check-ins.

The project aims to make health information easier to review and wellbeing activities more engaging. We built it with JavaScript, React, Three.js, Python, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL. We considered ease of use, local operation, and avoiding pressure in the game. Because we did not obtain a complete dataset or connect real sensors, the current readings are simulated and the health review rules are demonstrations. Vest measurements and exercise rewards are planned future additions.
